record.original_question: Do all monomial ideals in the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^n, 0) lie in the closure of the curvilinear locus?

evidence.quote: (Solved) problem XXX. Do all monomial ideals in Hilbd(A^n, 0) lie in the closure of the curvilinear locus?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $n\ge 1$ and $d\ge 1$ be integers, and let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$ denote the punctual Hilbert scheme parameterizing ideals $I\subset k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]$ (equivalently $0$-dimensional subschemes of $\mathbb{A}^n$ supported at the origin) such that $\dim_k k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]/I = d$. A point $[I]\in\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$ is called curvilinear if the quotient $k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]/I$ embeds into $k[[t]]$, equivalently if $I$ contains the maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ to a power and the quotient is generated by a single element as a $k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]$-module; equivalently $\mathrm{Spec}\,k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]/I$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{Spec}\,k[t]/(t^d)$. The curvilinear locus $\mathrm{Curv}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)\subset\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$ is the locally closed subset of curvilinear points. A monomial ideal is an ideal generated by monomials in $x_1,\dots,x_n$.

Question: Does every monomial ideal $I\in\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$ lie in the Zariski closure of the curvilinear locus $\mathrm{Curv}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as solved in the compilation of open problems where it appears. Standard references on punctual Hilbert schemes (Briançon, Iarrobino, and subsequent work) establish that every monomial ideal degenerates to a curvilinear ideal, so every monomial point lies in the closure of the curvilinear locus.
